Keywords: Wrecked cargo salvage and competing rights
RagShortTexts: Wrecked cargo involves owners, salvors and shore claimants.
Rescue costs and compensation require specific negotiation.

Variants.Content: A wreck creates rescue, salvage and ownership disputes together. Owners, shore holders and helpers make claims. Guarding recovered goods and witnessing recovery help distinguish ownership and reasonable carriage costs.
Wreck guards protect people and count recovered goods. Private taking compromises rescuers and the shore’s reputation with future traders.
Protecting merchants builds port credit while salvors need payment. Defined custody and adjudication reduce conflict better than unrestricted claims of custom.
Shore helpers risk themselves and working time while owners may have lost a vessel. Witnessed damage and custody help both sides negotiate compensation.
